images.caption: Figure 1:Overview of Embodied Agent Arena. Each row illustrates six tasks in one capability domain, spanning camera and scene estimation, spatial relations, functional grounding, goal-directed planning, and robot manipulation. Fixed-input probes test estimates and judgments; interactive episodes test goal completion. Spatial-tracing overlays show reference paths and a 3D target region.

Figure 2:Construction of the 1,000-case arena. (a) Representative task vocabulary across sources. (b) Five-domain composition, including 112 spatial-tracing cases in Geometry. (c) GeoProbe case counts for calibration, pose, depth, displacement, and scale. (d) Source queries, scenes, and targets form cases for a shared agent–environment loop; state persists between rounds, and native criteria determine termination and scoring. Colors identify domains; logos denote source institutions.

images.caption: Figure A5:Geometry: displacement, reference frames, and trajectories.Selected first-run predictions. (a) The jug moves right by 2 cm relative to the table. (b) Camera translation uses camera A’s frame, with reference[12,9,0][12,9,0]cm; orientation is omitted. (c) TraceSpatial paths are projected into the image; the errors are 3D Fréchet distances in meters, distinct from aggregate trajectory RMSE. Reference, Astra, Fable, and Opus 5.5 paths are drawn, with all nine errors listed.

Figure A6:Spatial Reasoning: errors depend on the reference frame.Selected first-run answers without YOLOE. (a) MindCube asks about camera movement between two views: A is diagonally forward-right, B right, C left, and D diagonally forward-left. (b) MMSI-Bench displays two selected views from its multi-view input and asks for a direction anchored to the open cupboard: A is northwest, B southwest, C north, and D northeast. (c) 3DSRBench asks which side of the person faces the camera: A is front, B left, C back, and D right. Green letters match the source reference; red letters do not. Different agents succeed on different frame transformations.

Figure A7:Affordance: region shape and target identity are separate challenges.Direct polygon outputs on the same UMD, ReasonAff, and RAGNet tasks. Green fill is the reference mask; colored native contours are model predictions. Each row uses one shared crop for the reference, Astra, Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5, andDeepSeek-1017. IoU is computed over the full original image, not the crop. (a) Scissor outlines differ in extent and alignment. (b) Handle contours cover only part of the annotated pulling region. (c) Agents select different objects under the two-hand instruction. These are single-run examples; the project-page gallery provides all ten models, full images, and recorded polygon coordinates.

Figure A8:Task Planning: a terminal episode need not be a completed task.Additional Opus 5.5 runs. (a) ALFWorld reports success after 8 code rounds under ceilings of 20 minutes, 8 rounds, 120 environment steps, 540 primitive calls, and 320k tokens. (b) DiscoveryWorld reports success after 7 rounds under 20 minutes, 8 rounds, 100 steps, 400 calls, and 320k tokens; its text/JSON interaction is illustrated with environment snapshots. (c) HumanCLAW stops after 70 rounds (933.6 s) without completing the couch-sitting task, under ceilings of 180 minutes, 101 rounds, 100 steps, 400 calls, and 2M tokens. The HumanCLAW episode ends in task failure before the time ceiling. Frames sample saved observations at discrete times.

Figure A9:Manipulation: motion can continue without completing all goals.Additional Opus 5.5 runs through recorded source-native interfaces. (a) CALVIN sequence 0526 reports success; (b) sequence 0557 exhausts 40 model rounds. Both allow 7,000 primitive calls and 1.28M tokens. (c) LIBERO-PRO requires placing a mug inside the microwave and closing it; the run exhausts 24 model rounds, with ceilings of 256 primitive calls and 640k tokens. Outcomes come from the terminal reports. Frame labels index the encoded recording, whereas the seconds beside each outcome are wall-clock runtime. The three panels illustrate distinct task instances and source interfaces.

Figure A10:Nine-model task execution in ALFRED.Each panel shows the first and last displayed observations from an individual Baseline episode, with a shortened instruction, terminal outcome, rounds, and wall-clock runtime. All runs allow 8 model rounds, 120 environment steps, and 20 minutes.DeepSeek-1017exhausts 8 rounds on the same spray-bottle task as Astra. The two Qwen models in panels (f,g) share the remote-and-lamp task:Qwen-397Breports success after 5 rounds, whereasQwen-27Bexhausts its budget at 8. Other panels cover separately selected tasks. Saved observations preserve temporal order with unequal intervals.

Figure A11:Subgoal scores and task outcomes after code errors.Matching saved observations and native score histories for one DiscoveryWorld archaeology task. Crosses mark rounds containing code errors; a score of 1 accompanies native success in these records. The two images are the first and last saved frames of each observation replay; they are not synchronized with the adjacent round axis. All three runs allow 8 model rounds, 100 environment steps, 400 primitive calls, 320k tokens, and 20 minutes.

Figure A12:The same drawer task separates activity from completion.First, middle, and last frames from each model’s matched RoboCasa clip, in temporal order. Opus 5.5 andDeepSeek-1017exhaust their budgets; Gemini 4 Argon completes the task. All three allow 24 model rounds, 256 primitive calls, and 1.12M tokens. The common task timeout is 60 minutes; Gemini 4 also records an 80-minute outer timeout. Clips cover selected portions of execution, not the complete wall-clock runtime. Outcomes use the terminal reports.

Figure A13:Satisfying the orientation tolerance does not ensure insertion.Matching ManiSkill PlugCharger-v1 clips, sampled at their first, middle, and last frames. Opus 5.5 ends in task failure;DeepSeek-1017and Gemini 4 Argon exhaust their budgets. All allow 32 model rounds, 1,024 primitive calls, 640k tokens, and a 60-minute task timeout; Gemini 4 records a 74-minute outer timeout. Opus reaches the native 400-step episode limit. The frames illustrate execution; the numerical distances and angles in the text come from terminal verification.
